title: Introducing Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion
format_note: Presenter voiceover over a screen-recorded story: a bike-share dashboard becomes an animated film, then comments and export are shown, ending on a typed tagline and logo.
one_thing: The film is its own demo: the animation about empty bike docks that the voiceover opens with is the product's output, and the interface shown wrapping it is the proof.

transcript.voice_style: Relaxed first-person presenter, conversational, short sentences, a worked story told in first person ('Pretend that I run the operations team').
transcript.script_shape: Teaser line, name the two products, a bike-share scenario, dashboard, turn it into animation, steer with comments, share and export, product names again, try today.

structure.frame0: Full-frame 3D isometric city map, 6:10 am clock chip top-left, two white station labels (Fernhill 21 bikes, Canal Street 6 bikes). Subject present, not black or logo (f0001.jpg).
structure.first_3s: The finished animation plays full-frame, a station label pops in within 0.25 s (strips/window-01-0s.jpg), then shrinks into a player frame at t=2 s with a scrub bar (f0002.jpg).

beats.what: Finished 3D bike-map animation plays full-frame, then pulls back into a video player chrome while voice says it is about empty bike docks.
Player scrubs back from the dashboard, then cuts to the presenter on camera inside the same player frame.
Presenter introduction with name, team and demos-recorded cards sliding in beside the video (f0005.jpg).
Title card in the player: Introducing Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion, with a bike travelling a timeline and three chart cards beside it.
Presenter in a red shirt; a comment thread builds on the video, joke that he changed outfits, showing comments on video.
Data-source logos (AWS, BigQuery, ClickHouse, Databricks, Salesforce, Snowflake) slide in a row: where the data comes from.
Claude chat creates the Bike Share System Overview dashboard, then the page scrolls with chart tooltips and a station map.
Map card selected, comment typed asking Claude to turn it into an animation, then text-led build steps and the Motion artifact appears.
38-second 3D bike film: night to morning, station labels, routes, then a camera drop to the empty dock row.
Comment on the video is sent, Claude updates the artifact, then colleagues' comments and a drawn circle appear on the player.
Export button and ten design-tool logos orbit it: export straight into design tools.
Typed tagline Claude makes it. You steer it. is selected and edited like a text box.
Claude asterisk and wordmark build and hold to the end.

hero_moment.what: The 3D city film at 6:50 am: Fernhill 17 bikes label, teal routes, then the camera drops to the dock row (f0028.jpg, f0029.jpg).

ending.cta_text: Claude makes it. You steer it.
ending.what: Cursor-edited tagline then the Claude logo builds letter by letter and holds on a cream ground for about 3.6 s, final 4 s static.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: Slow, continuous change inside long shots (longest 31.8 s, 38.9 % of runtime, the dashboard and comment scroll) with eight hard cuts only; no burst. Most change comes from elements sliding in the player or UI state changes.

look.ground: Warm off-white cream with a faint dot grid for the player scenes; the 3D film is a soft pastel miniature city under a wide-angle tilt.
look.accent_use: Amber marks the hill problem and teal the downtown surplus in both dashboard and film; coral appears only on Claude-owned elements (asterisk, Send, Export).
look.type: Serif (Tiempos-like) for titles, tagline and logo; condensed bold grotesque for the film's clock and labels; clean sans for interface text; monospace for the filename above the player.
look.depth: The 3D film has real parallax, long cast shadows and a depth-of-field blur; everything inside the player is flat with a single hard black outline.

product_ui.camera_on_ui: Mostly locked full-frame screen captures of the app; one scroll-and-zoom of the dashboard at 30-37 s; comment cards slide in at larger scale than they appear in the real app.
product_ui.notes: Dashboard text (KPI captions, chart axes) is about 8-11 px tall on a 720 frame and unreadable at phone width, but the large KPI numerals 445K, 2,999, 21%, 4,200, 71%, 92 and the enlarged comment cards are legible (crops/kpis.png, crops/prompt.png).

motion.text_entry: Tagline types in as a text box with a selection and toolbar (strips/window-50-73.542s.jpg); logo builds letter by letter at 24 fps (strips/window-53-77.709s.jpg); the build-step line reveals word by word.
motion.ui_motion: Elements spring in: comment cards grow downward as replies add, logo tiles slide in a row, ten tiles orbit the Export button. Scrub bar head follows the film's own time and wipes pink segments.
motion.camera: The 3D film has a slow tilted drift, then a drop to street level at the dock row; the player scenes are locked-off.
motion.eases: Out-heavy easing with small overshoot on cards and tiles; cursor glides on curved paths; eases judged by eye from strips, not measured.

transitions.cause: Comment is sent, map card is replaced by the build-step text card.
Chat panel slides over the film as the comment is sent.
Full-frame film shrinks into a player frame holding the same picture.
Logo tiles slide across, pushing off the right edge toward the dashboard.
Camera drops from overhead city to the dock row at street level.

on_screen_lines.text: 6:10 am Typical weekday; Fernhill 21 bikes; Canal Street 6 bikes
Introducing Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion
@Claude did Nate change outfits here? Yes, at 0:14 he switches to an orange shirt. I'm method acting!
Create a dashboard from a year of our ride data. The docks on the hill are empty by 8:15 every weekday...
@Claude turn this into an animation ... keep it simple: the hill running dry by 8:15, and the 92 bikes we carry back up.
Projecting dashboard coordinates into a 3D city grid
Tracing every morning ride from the hilltop to downtown
@Claude Hold on the empty dock a beat longer so it lands.
Can we name the van route here? Ops will ask. / Love the 4,200. Put it on the all-hands title slide too. / Hold on...
Claude makes it. You steer it.

good.observation: The film demonstrates the product by being its output: the opening 3D animation is the thing the story later builds, so the payoff is already in frame 0.
good.evidence: f0001.jpg opens on the Motion output; f0027-f0029 show it built.

good.observation: A single metaphor frame (a video player with scrub bar and filename) holds every scene, so changes of subject read as the same world.
good.evidence: f0002.jpg to f0014.jpg, f0034.jpg, f0035.jpg share the player chrome.

good.observation: Consistent colour semantics: amber is the hill problem, teal the surplus, in the dashboard and in the animation.
good.evidence: f0017.jpg dashboard map vs f0001.jpg film markers.

good.observation: Story data is reduced to a few legible numbers: the 33-word prompt names only 8:15 and 92 bikes, and the film shows those two.
Real product screens (chat, Share button, comments) are shown rather than invented, while the heavily simplified overlays are scaled up for legibility.
The ending cleans the screen: tagline typed in an editor box, then a logo that builds letter by letter and holds 3.6 s on cream.

weak.observation: A 24 s on-camera presenter section opens the film before the product shows; the jokes (outfit change, demos recorded 17) add time without selling.
Dashboard interface text is tiny: the chart axes and KPI sublines are unreadable at phone width and the camera only scrolls past them.
Pace is slow and uneven: 8 hard cuts, no burst, a 31.8 s longest shot and a 4 s static end.

rule_candidates.rule: Open on the finished product output full-frame, then shrink it into an interface frame; the film's frame 0 is the payoff, not a setup.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0001.jpg full-frame film; f0002.jpg at t=2 s inside player.

rule_candidates.rule: Use one container (player, window) for the whole film and move between subjects by changing what is inside it, so cuts read as state changes rather than new scenes.
rule_candidates.evidence: 8 cuts in 82 s; player chrome in 10 frames of the 41.

rule_candidates.rule: A film can run 4.75 s median shots and 5.9 cuts/min, with no burst, when change is carried by UI state; the 1.8-3.5 s cut rhythm is not required for feature explainers.
Scale up a UI fragment (comment card, prompt box) to fill 40 percent or more of frame width at the moment the viewer must read it, rather than showing the full-app screen.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0021.jpg prompt box ~520 px of 1280; f0016.jpg full dashboard unreadable.

rule_candidates.rule: Give each data colour one job across the whole film: one colour for the problem, one for the contrast, coral only for brand-owned controls.
rule_candidates.evidence: amber and teal in f0017.jpg and f0001.jpg; coral on Send and Export, f0021.jpg, f0035.jpg.

rule_candidates.rule: End on a typed tagline in an edit box followed by a letter-by-letter logo that holds 3 s or more on a clean ground.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0036-f0039 tagline, f0040-f0041 logo; metrics longest_static_run_s 4.

rule_candidates.rule: Keep voice-over at about 155 words per minute and let the on-screen prompt text carry names and numbers while the voice carries the story.
rule_candidates.evidence: transcript 212 words over 82 s; prompt text in crops/prompt.png.
